title: Feedback trading
author: yukajii
selftext:
You know there used to be a follow for follow thing? I propose feedback for feedback. Not to ramp up the numbers on some platform - to get playtesting feedback from fellow builders.

I drop a link to my game, you reply with a link to yours. We both play each other's games and post our feedback in replies. We both give it a decent play, 5-10 minutes at least, not a 30 second gloss-over. And post constructive feedback here, a paragraph or two of what you liked and didn't like.

No cherry picking, you see a thread without a reply - you reply to it with your link and review. No empty threads - start a new one by replying to the main post.

If you want feedback on a specific part of the game - mention it, but know it's to bring attention to something, not guarantee a result.

I hope this kind of reciprocal input can be more productive than simply dropping a link to your game or art asking for opinions. 

And if you don't have a game available but want to give feedback - no one would mind I guess, so feel free to participate.

replies.author: yukajii
replies.body:
https://i.redd.it/zjzgmrzw910i1.png

I got to score 45k, here's my feedback:

1. I like the unhinged style, visually it's pretty cool.  
2. Animations are barely there. The main character moves back and forth when hitting, but he could at least raise his arm/weapon.  
3. It's anything but idle, the auto attack perk is on the third page, and it's not clear how to get PP.  
4. The little guys running around have no clear purpose, killing them doesn't seem to do anything.  
5. Having achievements is pretty cool :)

replies.author: ThomasDuder
replies.body:
Yeah, I kinda want the player dropped into the action in media res, just like 13 himself.  No tutorial, however... it's not clear how to get perk points.  THAT is something I shall address, yah!

Once my balance gets refreshed, I'm more focusing on increasing the sfx versus bosses.  Still, more animations...hmmm.  I'll see what I can do.

The auto slash versus accessibility auto slash is something I'm fine tuning.  As an accessibility feature it's so those with injuries or disabilities can still play, however it disabled the feature as a perk.  I'll work on how to differentiate/clarify it for the player....

Thanks for the invaluable feedback!  I genuinely appreciate it, yo. :)

comments.author: RocketGruntJake
comments.body:
I recently built a demo version of my larger Unity Game to host as an HTML web build. I’d love some feedback on that demo specifically and whether it makes you want to download the whole game.

https://daddio-retro.itch.io/tailout

This is Tailout, a one button, high-octane slot car racing game. Build and race the slot car tracks you made as a kid! It supports 4 players on a single screen and up to 8 in online lobbies. The web demo on itch has local play against competent bots, up to 4 players on a single screen, and features the new hot lap leaderboard. A single track and car that rotates weekly with a built-in leaderboard system that runs through the server.

Try it out and post a time for the this weeks 5 lap race of driftwood on mixing bowl. Try and beat my time Jake-Dev… 

It does play best with a controller, also supports mobile browser play with a touch interface.

Let me know what you think!

replies.author: RocketGruntJake
replies.body:
Played to the golem boss so far. 

Tap is much easier to move the character than drag. I feel my finger is blocking my view how I would hold my phone.

I like the concept and the graphics. I think some balancing would help, my thought is that the boom upgrade is unreasonably strong. 

The boss battle is a fun take on the base game concept. When I get the pick caught up behind the boss and it bounces off the top of the screen and between the boss I expect it to count each hit. But only every other or so actually damages.

Selecting where to go in between rounds can also be made clearer. It started on the treasure chest then went down to the boss for example and I did not expect that.

I didn’t play with audio as a note

I’ll keep chugging along a bit to get more impressions

replies.author: yukajii
replies.body:
Thank you!

The difficulty does seem to be an issue, true. 

By "only every other or so actually damages" do you mean some hits on the boss don't do damage? Or did you expect it to count bounces off the edge of the screen?

replies.author: RocketGruntJake
replies.body:
On the golem first boss of the pickaxe bounces between it and the top of the level not every hit did damage.

Played through the next act, difficulty is definitely something to balance to. I never felt challenged. The yeti boss on act three I literally did nothing and still beat it without loosing life. I played from yeti to magma trying to lose but could not figure out how to lose. So I think the difficulty is where you can work to make the game more interesting. When I died on 26 I still am not entirely clear how or why. 

I played a second delve with the rune of time character and figured out it’s when your axe hits the ground. When you have multiple axes does only the original damage you when it hits the ground? That may be where I got confused.

Also a way to preview the route to see what each stop along the varying paths would help me make my decision on which way to go in each act.

replies.author: yukajii
replies.body:
I actually found a bug thanks to your feedback: bosses have a short period of immortality between hits so they don't melt if pickaxe gets stuck. I will shorten it.

And yes, mid-game needs balancing.

replies.author: yukajii
replies.body:
It was surprisingly good! I'm way behind you at 47 seconds, and I haven't managed a single 5-lap run without deslotting a dozen times.

1. I was confused about the controls at first. Not sure if it was some kind of glitch. In a "one button game" I expect to use spacebar, but it didn't work. Then I grabbed controller, and at first it wasn't doing anything for some reason, I started using stick, and only later got the trigger working. And only after all that I touched the spacebar and it also worked.  
2. On a related note, the menu is a bit confusing. E.g. to restart a hot lap you need to specifically end the run in the menu.  
3. I made quite a few laps, but I don't feel when the speed is too much and I will deslot. I guess it comes with more experience.

I'm not huge on racing, but this one felt really quite good. It would need to have a meta progression to retain me, but I can see it becoming an almost meditative experience when you can smoothly go lap after lap feeling the flow.

replies.author: RocketGruntJake
replies.body:
Thanks for the feedback!

The game is best played couch coop style or online racing friends.

It really plays poorly with just keyboard control since the whole game is built around the idea of throttle control.

The gamepad should have rumble feedback. That combined with the throttle control of a trigger is how you make it through turns effectively. You really never have to let up the throttle complexly and feather the trigger either pressing more when you drive down a straight or letting up as you enter a turn. 

You are right it is almost a rhythm game once you get a feel for the controls.

I will have to work out a way to better onboard someone to the feel of the controls and push them to use a controller or touch controls over the spacebar controls.

The menu is meant to be represented by physical items in the setting (80s basement) for a very immersive feel. I will have to make some of that more clear somehow.

replies.author: yukajii
replies.body:
I'm using a pretty old xbox one controller that was through a lot, so maybe its haptics are just off.

As for the menu - it does feel pretty authentic, and I could get used to it for sure, esp. in a full game. It does have a very immersive feel. One thing that might clear the UI with little effort is if you detect which device is currently being used and change the tooltips to either keyboard or gamepad, instead of showing / both.

replies.author: RocketGruntJake
replies.body:
Yeah the haptics on computers vs consoles is such a headache. For example I use a ds4 and that wireless has no rumble on a Mac but plugged in with rumble. 

It really plays best on a gamepad with rumble! I’ve contemplated building my own controller to mimic the controllers actually used for slot car racing with rumble and the simple one-trigger control for a true authentic experience.

The full game does that with the UI prompts, I’ll make sure it is in the demo build, that may have been an oversight. 

Ultimately from your feedback I have decided to cut the spacebar control/keyboard control as the game is nearly unplayable without some way to control the throttle beyond on/off like you get with the keyboard button press. I’m working on a mouse slide throttle control for those without a keyboard but will heavily prompt the player to plug in a gamepad.

replies.author: yukajii
replies.body:
Played on mouse + keyboard

The style is cute, the sounds are simple but nice. The ruthless world of gulls if also pretty cool :)

It is quite difficult though. You get a tutorial and then you're thrown into action with 3 different tasks per level, each of them having multiple repetitions. I honestly could not progress past level 2 in around 6 attempts, always at least one task not done, the toddler not crying, or Gary dodging my dives.

Also, for some reason I assumed the dives were only vertical, and kept crashing. Only on 3rd attempt I realized it works much better when the angle is not that steep.

So yeah I would love a more staggered rollout of mechanics and tasks, maybe let me dive-steal some ice creams first, and them fight the gulls in another level, and then take sweets for babies :)

The pick ups and bonnussess work well and make sense! I don’t have much to add really, it feels quite finished and polished visually and gameplay wise, so congrats on making this!
